extracted.intended_audience: SBIR/STTR participating agency program managers, SBA staff, and policymakers (also stakeholders such as small businesses and program evaluators)
extracted.subtask_description: Agency-level reporting and compliance guidance for SBIR/STTR programs including timeline performance metrics, requirements for Administrative Funding Pilot Program (AFPP) work plans and reporting, commercialization pilot program rules (CRP/CRPP), Phase III definition and tracking, and outreach/selection practices to increase participation by underrepresented firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy Directive award notification timeline (<= 90 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Policy Directive prescribes the duration between the closing date of the solicitation and the notification of recommendation of award of no more than 90 calendar days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied as a performance requirement for STTR (and SBIR) award processing. The report notes agency compliance (e.g., Army and ODAs met this notification requirement for 100% of STTR Phase I awards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Average time between Phase I Solicitation Close and Award Notification (days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric tracked per agency: average number of days between Phase I solicitation close and award notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in tables and charts by agency (civilian and DoD). Used with percentage thresholds to evaluate timeliness of award notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average time between Phase I Notification and First Day of Period of Performance (days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric tracked per agency: average number of days between Phase I award notification and the first day of the award's period of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in tables/charts; used to evaluate how quickly awardees can begin work after notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I: percentage with Solicitation Close → Notification <= 90 days (exceptions for HHS/NSF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of Phase I awards where time between solicitation close and notification was less than or equal to 90 days (1 year for HHS and NSF only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a compliance/timeliness benchmark in agency reporting; HHS and NSF have different allowance noted in the dataset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I: percentage with Solicitation Close → First Day of Performance <= 180 days (exceptions for HHS/NSF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of Phase I awards where time between solicitation close and the first day of performance was less than or equal to 180 days (15 months for HHS and NSF only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance metric for time-to-start; reported by agency and used to assess administrative efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average time between Phase I award final day and Phase II award first day
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric tracked per agency: average number of days between Phase I award final day of period of performance and Phase II award's first day of period of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess continuity/transition between Phase I and Phase II work; reported by agency (large variances highlighted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Average time between Phase II Solicitation Close/Proposal Receipt and Award Notification (days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric tracked per agency: average number of days between Phase II solicitation close date or proposal receipt date and award notification date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in tables/charts; paired with percentage thresholds to evaluate Phase II processing timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II: percentage with Solicitation Close/Proposal Receipt → Notification <= 90 days (exceptions for HHS/NSF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of Phase II awards where time between solicitation close or proposal receipt and notification date was less than or equal to 90 days (1 year for HHS and NSF only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an outcome metric to gauge Phase II award processing speed; reported by agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II: percentage with Solicitation Close/Proposal Receipt → First Day of Performance <= 180 days (exceptions for HHS/NSF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of Phase II awards where time between solicitation close or proposal receipt and first day of performance was less than or equal to 180 days (450 days or 15 months for HHS and NSF only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance benchmark for phase transition timeliness; used in agency comparisons and compliance assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: AFPP: work plan submission and required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Agencies are required to submit a work plan for SBA approval to use the Administrative Funding Pilot Program (AFPP) authority. The work plan must include the specific activities to be supported, the estimated costs for the activities, milestones, and the expected results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AFPP authority permits using up to 3% of SBIR funding for administrative/oversight/contract processing costs; SBA reviews work plans and agencies must report obligations and outcomes annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: AFPP: permissible activities and intended uses
rubrics_metrics.description: AFPP funds are to support initiatives to improve the program and the experience for small businesses, including updating/upgrading IT systems for new reporting, modifying application/review/selection processes to shorten award timelines, developing targeted marketing and commercialization plans, assessing prior awardee commercialization efforts, and continuing outreach to underrepresented communities to increase small business participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies provided concrete examples of how AFPP funds were used (IT upgrades, centralized contracting offices to reduce award times, Phase 0 services, targeted marketing).

rubrics_metrics.name: AFPP: required reporting/performance areas
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the annual report submission, SBA requires agencies to report AFPP obligations and performance criteria outcomes organized into: (1) Outreach; (2) Commercialization; (3) Streamlining and Simplification; (4) Prevention and Detection of Fraud, Waste, and Abuse; (5) Reporting; and (6) Administration and Implementation of Reauthorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must present obligations and outcomes under these six areas; used by SBA to evaluate AFPP effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to report outreach to underrepresented businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Agency is required to report its efforts to increase outreach and awards to firms owned and controlled by women or by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals, and to firms in underrepresented (IDeA) states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report includes agency-specific outreach activities and metrics (e.g., numbers of events, Phase 0 participants, demographics of assisted firms). Agencies describe outreach programs and targeted campaigns; some agencies incorporate outreach considerations into selection processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection priority / consideration for SDBs and WOSBs (agency practice example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technically excellent proposals received from SDBs and WOSBs (and SDBs/WOSBs from HUBZones and underserved states) are one of several selection criteria within NIST’s Phase I selection process; NOAA plans to implement a similar process to give priority to technically excellent proposals from SDBs and WOSBs in future evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may include outreach/priority approaches in solicitation and selection criteria to promote participation by underrepresented firms; this is presented as an operational selection practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRP (DoD): purpose, permitted uses, and funding cap
rubrics_metrics.description: The DoD Commercialization Readiness Program (CRP) pays for activities that accelerate the transition of DoD SBIR/STTR-funded technologies to Phase III, especially those with significant benefit to warfighters. Under the CRP, up to 1% of the available SBIR funding may be used by DoD Service Agencies and ODAs for payment of expenses incurred to support CRP activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRP funds activities that enhance connectivity among SBIR/STTR firms, prime contractors, and DoD science & technology and acquisition communities; DoD provides a CRP report describing activities and firms helped under CRP funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRP legislative requirements for DoD (15 U.S.C. § 638(y))
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory requirements authorized DoD to: establish goals for the transition of Phase III technologies in subcontracting plans; require a prime contractor on such a contract to report the number and dollar amount of contracts entered into by that prime contractor for Phase III SBIR/STTR projects for efforts over $100,000,000; set a goal to increase the number of Phase II SBIR and STTR contracts that lead to technology transition into programs of record or fielded systems; and use incentives to encourage agency program managers and prime contractors to meet these goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA notes DoD has not fully implemented these requirements (no data provided on number/percentage of Phase IIs leading to transition, CRP project statuses, goals or incentives). This legislative standard is a compliance expectation for DoD.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRPP (Civilian agencies): authority, caps, and award size limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Civilian Agency Commercialization Readiness Pilot Program (CRPP) allows an agency to use up to 10% of its SBIR/STTR budget for additional awards to SBIR/STTR awardees. The size of these awards may be up to three times the Phase II guideline amount. Once an agency submits and has its CRPP plan approved by SBA, it does not have to reapply year to year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report provides table summarizing CRPP activity (number of awards and amounts) and describes agency-specific CRPP uses and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRPP reporting/accounting requirement (15 U.S.C. § 638(b)(7)(F))
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Agencies must provide an accounting of funds, initiatives, and outcomes under the CRPP to SBA, as required by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies summarize CRPP activities and obligations to SBA in annual reporting; SBA reviews CRPP compliance and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase III: definition and reporting limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase III is defined as work that derives from, extends, or completes Phase I or II work and is not supported by SBIR or STTR dollars. Agencies cannot use SBIR/STTR funding for Phase III awards. Phase III reporting is limited because agencies and firms often do not document SBIR/STTR lineage of follow-on funding and small businesses are not required to notify program offices about Phase III funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA recognizes reporting will undercount true Phase III funding. Agencies are encouraged to increase Phase III funding provided by themselves or through FFRDCs, and to improve tracking mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices to encourage Phase III transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should identify and fund SBIR/STTR Phase I and II work with a transition path into a program or platform; align awards with agency customers to encourage Phase III commercialization and ensure projects reach desired Technology Readiness Level (TRL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report cites the Navy’s long-standing practice of aligning SBIR/STTR projects with transition paths into programs of record as an example. SBA recommends implementing goals, incentives, and reporting (per statutory guidance) to increase transitions.
